core.title: Name e2e specs with the stack's e2e-test name pattern
core.given: A file is recognised as an end-to-end spec by content: it imports the stack's e2e test framework and declares tests (how the e2e-test role is assigned comes from the profile).
core.when: The file is created, renamed or edited (including an existing arbitrarily named file gaining a test declaration), or the tree is scanned.
core.then: Name it with the stack's e2e-test name pattern (from the profile), whatever its prior name or extension.
prefer: Rename a misnamed e2e spec to the e2e-test pattern and point the e2e runner's file selection at that pattern.
Keep the two runners apart: the unit/acceptance test runner runs unit, acceptance and smoke tests; the e2e runner runs only browser specs; neither picks up the other's files.
avoid: Naming an e2e spec with a unit- or acceptance-test name pattern — the unit/acceptance test runner collects it and runs it with the wrong runner.
Hiding a misnamed e2e spec from the unit/acceptance test runner with an ad-hoc filter instead of renaming it.
unless: Vendored and generated trees are never scanned.
Files that are not recognised as e2e specs (no e2e-framework import and test declarations) are out of scope.
The e2e runner's configuration file (its name pattern from the profile), and fixture modules that only extend the test-declaration surface without declaring tests, are out of scope.
core.why: The unit/acceptance test runner collects files by its own unit- and acceptance-test name patterns, so an e2e spec named that way runs under the wrong runner and fails, or worse is skipped by a filter nobody remembers.
evidence: Every non-excluded file recognised as an e2e spec matches the e2e-test name pattern, whatever its prior name or extension.
The e2e runner's file selection targets the e2e-test pattern and the unit/acceptance test runner collects no browser spec.
verification: The check establishes that a file is an e2e spec from its content — e2e-framework import plus test declarations, per the profile's e2e-test role assignment — and inspects the content of every non-excluded file without pre-filtering by current name or extension, so a misnamed input is still detected; path or extension alone cannot establish the fact, and a content observer is required.
Independently of change events, a full-tree content scan also catches pre-existing violations that no current change touched.

This check owns its exact exclusion classification rather than deferring to the stack-wide excluded-roots list: vendored and generated trees are never scanned, and the e2e runner's configuration file (per the profile's config name pattern) and fixture modules that only extend the test-declaration surface without declaring tests are skipped; the exclusions scope the check only and never narrow which file names or extensions are otherwise inspected.

A test file bound to a user/system flow or journey artifact through the stack's header binding syntax is still judged as an e2e spec when misnamed, but that binding is identification context only, not an independent naming trigger — the naming obligation still requires the e2e-framework import and test declarations; a unit test that merely mentions such a URN inside a string is not an e2e spec.

fires: A newly created file recognised as an e2e spec is named with a unit- or acceptance-test pattern instead of the stack's e2e-test pattern.
An existing helper file that already imports the e2e framework is edited to add a test declaration and keeps a name outside the e2e-test pattern.
A test file bound to a user/system flow or journey artifact that imports the e2e framework and declares tests is named with a unit- or acceptance-test pattern instead of the e2e-test pattern.
An e2e spec whose name matches one of the e2e-test pattern's allowed variants is checked and passes.
doesNotFire: A file under a vendored or generated tree.
A unit or acceptance test that does not import the e2e framework, even if its header carries a user/system flow or journey binding.
The e2e runner's configuration file, or a fixture module that only extends the test-declaration surface and declares no tests.
A unit test that merely mentions a user/system flow or journey URN inside a string.

profileRequirements.meaning: How a file is assigned the e2e-test role by content, and that a file without that assignment is out of scope for this rule, not a violation.
profileRequirements.bunValue: imports `@playwright/test` AND declares `test(...)` or `test.describe(...)`; a file without both is out of scope

profileRequirements.meaning: The e2e-test file-name patterns an e2e spec must match (including allowed variants).
The unit-test name pattern the unit/acceptance test runner auto-collects; an e2e spec must not carry it.
The acceptance-test name pattern the unit/acceptance test runner auto-collects; an e2e spec must not carry it.
The name pattern of the e2e runner's configuration file, which this check skips.
The unit/acceptance test runner that auto-collects test files by name pattern and would run a misnamed e2e spec under the wrong runner.
profileRequirements.bunValue: `bun test` (runs unit, acceptance and smoke tests)

profileRequirements.meaning: The header syntax by which a test file binds itself to a user/system flow artifact (identification context for judging a misnamed spec).
The header syntax by which a test file binds itself to a journey artifact (identification context for judging a misnamed spec).

neutralityNotes: The obligation itself is fully neutral: an e2e spec must carry the stack's e2e-test name pattern so the unit/acceptance runner never collects it. Everything concrete instantiates from existing profile keys: the e2e-test role assignment by content (roles.assignment), the e2e-test name patterns (suffix.e2e_test), the unit- and acceptance-test patterns the runner auto-collects (suffix.unit_test, suffix.acceptance_test), the e2e runner's configuration-file name (suffix.config), the unit/acceptance runner (tooling.test_runner), and user-system-flow/journey header bindings (urn.binding.user-system-flow, urn.binding.journey). Per the audit, three things deliberately do NOT go through the profile: (1) this check owns its exact exclusion classification, so the concrete tree and config skips stay in core verification at role level plus bunOnly, not in the stack-wide roots.excluded key; (2) the detector's language scope is retained in the realization because tooling.languages documents production-source languages; (3) the e2e runner's selection target (Playwright's testMatch at `**/*.e2e.ts`) is a realization configuration distinct from the accepted filename variants and is preserved in bunOnly. Remaining realization details in bunOnly: detector and term ids (htmx_e2e_detector, browser_spec), the exact skip globs, and the stack's test-extension construct. Severity and disposition stay in core verification per the not-profile-keys rule.
